clips.title: Your First Node.js Web Server
clips.why: Builds a server with the built-in http module from an empty file: createServer, one function with req and res, and listen.
look: The handler function and its two objects, req and res.
How the response is written and then ended with res.end().
listen on a port, and what you see in the browser.
clips.after: The broker and the gateway are this same function grown carefully: a route string, a body limit and a status on every path.

clips.title: NodeJS APIs Without Express
clips.why: Routing by hand, without a framework, the way our services do it.
look: How the handler looks at the URL and the method to pick what to do, with no router library.
Compare it with the lesson's version, where every path, including an unknown one, ends with a status.
clips.after: Our version joins method and path into one string, such as POST /v1/comments, and ends with a 404 for everything else.

clips.title: HTTP Status Codes Explained In 5 Minutes
clips.why: A clear, animated tour of the status code families, so you can pick the right one on every path of a handler.
look: The 200s: success, including 201 Created for a new resource.
The 400s: the client's mistake, such as a bad request, a missing login or an unknown path.
clips.after: Callers and tests act on the status, so the broker answers 400, 401, 404 and 413 for the caller's mistakes and 500 only for its own.

practice.q: Your handler checks GET /health and POST /v1/comments, and any other request reaches the end of the function without an answer. What does a caller of GET /v1/nope experience?

options.why: Node has no routes of its own, so it cannot know the path is unknown.

options.text: A hanging request, until the caller stops waiting
options.why: The response ends only when your code calls res.end(). The lab's curl timed out after 3 seconds.
Nothing is sent at all, not even a status line, because end() is never called.

practice.q: Inside readBody, stop reading as soon as the body is too large.
practice.before:
size += chunk.length;
if (size > limit) throw new
practice.hint: Our own error class, so the handler can answer 413.
practice.why: Throwing inside the loop stops before the rest of the body is stored, and the catch turns TooLarge into 413.

practice.q: Which status fits a POST whose body is not valid JSON?

options.why: The request itself is wrong, and the caller can fix it. The catch maps the SyntaxError from JSON.parse to 400.
500 says the fault is ours, and sends people looking for a bug in the service.
413 means too large. The size is fine; the content is broken.

practice.q: Build the route string the handler compares against, from the request's method and the parsed URL.
practice.hint: The part of the URL without the query string.
practice.why: pathname is /v1/comments even when the URL is /v1/comments?limit=5, so the query does not break the route match.

practice.q: Put what happens to a 2 MB POST to /v1/comments in order.
items: Node calls the handler with req and res
The handler builds the route string POST /v1/comments
readBody counts chunks as they arrive
The count passes 1,048,576 bytes and readBody throws TooLarge
The catch answers 413, and the rest of the body is never stored
practice.why: The limit works because it is checked while the stream flows, not after the whole body is in memory.
